summary: Read the complete 524-line markdown, including references and author biographies; the 10-page paper has no appendix. Checked the four requested estimates against PDF pp. 5-8 (printed pp. 44-47), including Table 4 recovered with pymupdf.find_tables(); also checked the design and Figure 1 on PDF p. 4 and rater-related material on PDF pp. 9-10. All recorded statistics and counts match the printed values, outcomes, arm assignments, and gain or endpoint specifications. The 81 and 83 totals count the analyzed people in the two contrasted arms, as required by codebook section 7; the mixed model uses all 164 participants. The requested coding fields are supported: the contrasts are between randomized people within each initial-condition stratum, the treatment arms had AI during the same-session upgrade, the outcome is participant-level overall creativity, and larger scores mean greater creativity. The gain estimates use participant random effects; no endpoint-contrast uncertainty is printed, so their respective se_basis values are participant and not_reported. The four measure enum flags do not justify an extraction correction. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), section 3.2.4, states: "평가는 2명의 독립 평가자가 수행하였으며, 평가자는 참\n여자의 조건 정보를 알 수 없도록 한 상태에서 동일한 루브\n릭에 따라 채점하였다.". This confirms two independent blinded human evaluators, but neither this section nor the rest of the paper establishes their qualifications or lay/crowd status. Codebook section 6 defines human_raters as lay raters or crowd workers and expert_raters as domain experts, instructors, or professionals. Neither subtype can be confirmed; retain measure=null in all four estimates under the brief's instruction to use null for unconfirmed values. The enum warnings reflect the absence of an unknown-human-rater category, not evidence for a supported non-null replacement. No eligible outcome or contrast is missing under extraction rules 4-6: initial A/B randomization is not established; baseline balance checks and fixed-order within-arm changes are not randomized AI contrasts; H5 is moderation; fluency and rubric components have no reported arm-specific contrasts. Both eligible randomized arm pairs have gain and round-2 endpoint records.
